newsitem.title: UK: BZW says harsh price review may slow Rec dividends.
newsitem.headline: BZW says harsh price review may slow Rec dividends.

text.p: British regional electricity companies (Recs) may find dividend policies unsustainable if regulator Offer uses the same basis for their price review as he has for National Grid, according to BZW analyst Simon Taylor.

"Dividend policies do not look sustainable beyond 2000," he told Reuters on Monday, if Offer head Stephen Littlechild valued the asset base on market prices at flotation, as he did with National Grid, in the next Rec price review which comes in force in 2000.

Taylor said using the same basis of calculation for Recs and assuming a pretax real rate of return of seven percent compared with current Rec levels of 10-13 percent, "the financial position of the industry will tighten sharply."

He said that Offer, along with Ofgas and Ofwat, its cousins in gas and water respectively, had indicated in recent reviews that the asset base would be valued on market prices at flotation and not at book value.
That could mean "significant cuts in revenues and profits in 2000-2001," he added.
Taylor said these calculations would make the Recs look "a bit expensive...they are not all discounting a very severe pricing review in 2000."
He said Yorkshire Electricity and London Electricity in particular looked overvalued as a result.
London Electricity shares were down 3-1/2 pence at 0930 GMT to 598 pence while Yorkshire had fallen 5-1/2 pence to 747 pence with East Midlands Electricity down 7-1/2 pence to 505 pence.
But Taylor added the review might not follow similar lines to National Grid or companies might be able to find substantial further cost cuts in order to ease the impact of price curbs.
"We are seeing the maturing of the Recs," Taylor said.
